NASA Space Apps 2026 · Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots

One fire record. Two satellite eras.

SYNTRA merges 26 years of NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspots into one consistent record for Sudan, so a bad fire season looks bad because of fire, not because a sharper satellite arrived.

01 · 2001–2011

MODIS only

Terra and Aqua, 1 km pixels. Each bar is one month; years run back to front.

02 · 2012

VIIRS arrives

375 m pixels see far more fires. Joined raw, the record jumps ×2.5 overnight.

03 · Harmonize

Same units

A factor per calendar month, fitted on 2012–2021, lifts MODIS into VIIRS units.

04 · Validate

R² 0.993

On years the model never saw. Raw MODIS scores 0.36. The seam is gone.

Accuracy on years the model never saw

R² 0.36to0.993

Raw MODIS predicts what VIIRS saw with R² 0.36. After SYNTRA's harmonization: 0.993, tested leave-one-year-out on 119 months.

Under the hood

From raw pixels to a record you can plan with

DOWNLOAD4,462,802

clean hotspots, 2000–2026, from the FIRMS archive and the near-real-time API.

CLEAN45,464

always-hot sites set aside: gas flares, industry and other static heat sources.

HARMONIZE0.1°

fire cell-days: each grid cell counts once a day, then MODIS is converted month by month.

VALIDATER² 0.993

leave-one-year-out on 119 months. NOAA-20 × 0.986 takes over where Suomi NPP data ends.

Try it

Was that month normal?

Pick any month since 2001. SYNTRA compares it with the same month in every earlier year, the way the app's status card does.

Very high: above the 90th percentile. Above or below normal: 20% or more from the median.

Does it hold up?

Tested on years it never saw

119 held-out months per country. It works where vegetation burns. In Saudi Arabia, with few real fires and many gas flares, it does not, and we show that too.

CountryR² raw MODISR² harmonizedMedian annual error
Sudan0.360.992.4%
Ethiopia0.210.993.3%
Iraq0.260.917.8%
Saudi Arabia−13.7−0.9314.2%
